SYMPTOM: broadcast() in API routes silently no-ops. sessions Map is always empty in API routes. WebSocket server is null in API routes. Demo button works (200 OK) but nothing shows in browser.

CAUSE: Next.js App Router compiles API route handlers in its own module graph, separate from server.ts. Module-level variables (let wss, const sessions, const pending) exist in TWO separate instances. server.ts has the real WebSocket server; API routes have null/empty.

FIX APPLIED:
```typescript
// ws-server.ts
declare global { var __wss: WebSocketServer | undefined }
export function initWSS(server: HttpServer) {
  globalThis.__wss = new WebSocketServer({ server })
}
export function broadcast(data: unknown) {
  globalThis.__wss?.clients.forEach(client => { ... })
}

// store.ts
declare global { var __sessions: Map<string, Session> | undefined }
const sessions: Map<string, Session> = (globalThis.__sessions ??= new Map())

// approval-queue.ts  
declare global { var __pending: Map<string, PendingApproval> | undefined }
const pending = (globalThis.__pending ??= new Map())
```

WHY: globalThis is the Node.js global object, shared across all module instances in the same process.

GOTCHA: This affects ANY Next.js app using a custom server.ts with module-level singletons that API routes also need to access.
